summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would create a new federal agency to handle Australia's radioactive waste.
The agency would be a non-corporate Commonwealth entity with powers to manage waste and conduct activities at a designated facility.
The explanatory memorandum says the agency would also develop policy, give technical advice, educate the public, and keep a national inventory of radioactive material.
changes: Establishes the Australian Radioactive Waste Agency as a non-corporate Commonwealth entity.
Authorises the agency to manage controlled material and conduct activities under the National Radioactive Waste Management Act 2012.
Gives the agency functions including policy development, technical advice, public education, and maintaining a national inventory.
summary.affected: The agency and the Australian public, who benefit from nuclear medicine that produces the waste.

speeches.speaker: Keith Pitt
speeches.brief: The Australian Radioactive Waste Agency Bill 2022 transitions the agency from a departmental function to a separate non-corporate Commonwealth entity, establishing a dedicated body with a chief executive officer to manage the National Radioactive Waste Management Facility and oversee all stages of its design, construction, and operation.
